all.body:
This agreement is between **{{parties.employer_name}}** of {{parties.employer_address}} ("the Company", "we", "us") and **{{parties.worker_name}}** of {{parties.worker_address}} ("you").

It sets out the terms on which we may offer you casual work, and the terms that apply to each assignment you accept. You agree to do the work personally. From how the work is expected to happen, we have assessed you as a worker, not an employee. Status depends on what happens in practice, not on the words used, so we will review it with you if the way you work changes.

This agreement is also the written statement of particulars required by section 1 of the Employment Rights Act 1996, which applies to workers as well as employees. Schedule 1 (Key particulars) forms part of it.

all.body: This agreement starts on {{start.date}}. It stays in place until either of us ends it as set out in the clause on ending this agreement.

Your period of continuous employment began on {{start.continuous_date}}. Because this contract continues between assignments, weeks in which you do no work still count towards your continuous employment, as section 212 of the Employment Rights Act 1996 provides.

sources.title: nidirect: Employment contracts and written statement

all.body:
Each assignment you accept is a separate engagement on the terms of this agreement. Apart from any guaranteed hours set out in this agreement, neither of us has to offer or accept work between assignments.

Between assignments, this agreement stays in place only so that the same terms apply to any later assignment, and so that the clauses on confidentiality, personal data and returning property continue to apply.

sources.title: Labour Relations Agency: Types of contracts

all.body:
Your employment continues between assignments, including in weeks when you do no work. A gap between assignments does not end your employment. It only ends as set out in the clause on ending this contract.

Apart from any guaranteed hours set out in this contract, how work is offered and accepted is set out in the clauses on offers of work and availability. Your statutory rights as an employee continue to build up while this contract continues.

sources.title: Labour Relations Agency: Types of contracts

all.body:
Your role is **{{job.title}}**. On each assignment your main duties are: {{job.duties}}.

You report to {{job.reports_to}}, and on site to the supervisor or control room named in the assignment instructions. We will only offer you work that suits your skills, training and licence.

Assignments may be at {{place.locations}}. Each offer of work tells you the site. The Company's address in this agreement is your base for records and correspondence.

Time you spend travelling between sites during an assignment, at our request, is working time and is paid.

sources.title: GOV.UK: Calculating the minimum wage (travel time)

all.body: We do not guarantee you any hours of work. We offer work as and when it is available, and there may be weeks when we offer you none. Nothing in this agreement promises you a minimum amount of work or pay.

We guarantee you {{hours.guaranteed}} hours of paid work in each week. If we offer you fewer hours than that in a week, we will still pay you for the guaranteed hours, unless you turned down or did not attend work we offered you within them.

Work above the guaranteed hours is offered and accepted as set out in the clauses on offers of work and availability.

We offer work {{offer.channel}}, as far in advance as we reasonably can. Each offer tells you the site, the date, the start and finish times, the duties, the pay rate and any special requirements.

If you want the work, accept it {{offer.channel}} within {{offer.response}} of the offer. If you do not reply in that time, the offer lapses and we may offer the work to someone else. An assignment is agreed only when you have accepted the offer and we have confirmed it.

We keep a record of the offers we make you, and of each acceptance, confirmation and cancellation. You can ask to see your own record.

sources.title: Labour Relations Agency: Types of contracts

title: Availability: free to accept or refuse work
subject: casual

all.body:
You do not have to accept any work we offer, and you do not have to give a reason for turning work down. Turning down an offer will not be treated as misconduct and will not reduce the work we offer you in future.

You do not have to be available for work at any particular time.

You have agreed to be available for work {{availability.times}}. If we offer you work within those times, you should accept it unless you have a good reason not to, such as illness, caring responsibilities or other work you have already accepted.

Outside those times you may turn down any offer without giving a reason, and doing so will not reduce the work we offer you in future. You may ask to change your agreed availability at any time, and we will consider your request reasonably and reply in writing.

sources.title: GOV.UK: SIA standards of behaviour for security operatives

title: Cancellation and changes: booked hours paid
subject: casual

all.body:
We may need to cancel or shorten an assignment you have accepted. We will tell you {{offer.channel}} as soon as we know, and we aim to give you at least {{shift.cancel_notice}} notice. If we cancel or shorten an accepted assignment with less notice than that, we will pay you for the hours of the assignment as booked.

We will not change the date or times of an accepted assignment without your agreement. If you do not agree to a change, the assignment is treated as cancelled by us.

If you have already arrived at the site when an assignment is cancelled or cut short, we will always pay you for the time you were required to be there.

We may need to cancel or shorten an assignment you have accepted. We will tell you {{offer.channel}} as soon as we know, and we aim to give you at least {{shift.cancel_notice}} notice. If we cancel or shorten an accepted assignment with less notice than that, we will pay you {{shift.cancel_part}}.

We will not change the date or times of an accepted assignment without your agreement. If you do not agree to a change, the assignment is treated as cancelled by us.

If you have already arrived at the site when an assignment is cancelled or cut short, we will always pay you for the time you were required to be there.

title: Cancellation and changes: no cancellation payment
subject: casual

all.body:
We may need to cancel or shorten an assignment you have accepted. We will tell you {{offer.channel}} as soon as we know, and we aim to give you at least {{shift.cancel_notice}} notice. No cancellation payment is made for an assignment cancelled before you arrive at the site.

We will not change the date or times of an accepted assignment without your agreement. If you do not agree to a change, the assignment is treated as cancelled by us.

If you have already arrived at the site when an assignment is cancelled or cut short, we will always pay you for the time you were required to be there.

You must record your start and finish times {{time.method}}. Your pay is worked out from these records once they have been checked.

We pay you for all the time you are required to be at work, including briefings, handovers, training we require and travel between sites during an assignment. If a record of your time is wrong, tell us straight away so that it can be corrected before pay day.

sources.title: National Minimum Wage Regulations 2015, Part 5 (working time)

title: Pay: hourly rate for casual work
subject: casual

all.body:
We will pay you {{pay.rate}} for each hour you work, before tax and other deductions. You are paid {{pay.frequency}} in arrears by bank transfer, on {{pay.day}}, for the work you did in the pay period. You will receive an itemised payslip each time you are paid.

Your pay will never be lower than the National Minimum Wage or National Living Wage that applies to you, worked out over each pay reference period as the National Minimum Wage Regulations 2015 require. Any change to your rate will be confirmed to you in writing before you accept work at the new rate.

sources.title: GOV.UK: National Minimum Wage and National Living Wage rates

all.body: These enhanced rates or allowances also apply: {{pay.enhancements}}.

Your holiday year starts on {{holiday.year_start}}. Ask for holiday {{offer.channel}} at least {{holiday.notice}} in advance. We may refuse a request for operational reasons, or ask you to take holiday at particular times, by giving the notice the law requires.

When this agreement ends, we will pay you for holiday you have built up but not taken, unless you have already been paid for it.

title: Other leave and statutory payments: worker
subject: casual

all.body: Apart from holiday, there is no other paid leave under this agreement. Depending on your earnings and how long you have worked for us, you may qualify for statutory payments such as Statutory Maternity Pay, Statutory Paternity Pay, Statutory Adoption Pay, Statutory Shared Parental Pay and Statutory Parental Bereavement Pay. Ask us if you think one applies.

Our disciplinary rules and grievance procedure are in {{discipline.where}}. They follow the Acas Code of Practice on Disciplinary and Grievance Procedures and do not form part of this agreement. If you disagree with a disciplinary decision, you may appeal in writing to {{discipline.appeal_to}}.

If you have a concern about your work, raise it with {{grievance.raise_with}}, in writing if you can. You may be accompanied at a disciplinary or grievance hearing, as section 10 of the Employment Relations Act 1999 provides.

sources.title: Acas Code of Practice on disciplinary and grievance procedures

title: Work for others: free to work elsewhere
subject: casual

all.body:
You are free to work for other employers and businesses, including other security businesses, at any time. We will not treat you less favourably because you work elsewhere.

Please tell us if your other work could affect your rest breaks, rest periods or average weekly working time, so that we can meet our duties under the working time rules. Your duties of confidentiality under this agreement apply whoever else you work for.

sources.title: Labour Relations Agency: Types of contracts

title: Work for others: consent needed for other security work
subject: casual

all.body:
While this agreement continues, you must not work for another security business without our written consent. We will not refuse consent unreasonably, and we will give you our decision promptly. This does not stop you doing any other kind of work.

This clause does not apply, and will not be enforced, at any time when the law makes it unenforceable, for example while you have no guaranteed hours or your earnings are at or below the level the law protects.

all.body:
Either of us may end this agreement by giving {{ending.notice}} notice in writing. Assignments you have already accepted that fall within the notice period still go ahead and are paid, unless we cancel them as set out in the clause on cancellation and changes.

We may end this agreement straight away, without notice, for gross misconduct after following our disciplinary procedure, or if you no longer hold a licence your work needs or no longer have the right to work in the UK.

When this agreement ends, we will pay you for all work done and any holiday pay due, and you must return our property, uniform, keys, passes and documents.

Either of us may end this contract by giving notice in writing. You must give us {{ending.notice}} notice. We will give you {{ending.notice}} notice, or the statutory minimum notice in section 86 of the Employment Rights Act 1996 if that is longer: one week once you have been continuously employed for one month, rising to one week for each complete year of service, up to a maximum of twelve weeks.

Because this contract continues between assignments, it does not end just because no work has been offered or accepted for a while. We may pay you instead of some or all of your notice. We may end your employment without notice for gross misconduct, after following our disciplinary procedure.

When your employment ends, we will pay you for all work done and any holiday pay due, and you must return our property, uniform, keys, passes and documents.

all.body:
This agreement, including Schedule 1 and any documents it says form part of it, is the whole agreement between you and us about casual work. It replaces any earlier agreement or arrangement about that work. The confirmation of each assignment you accept forms part of this agreement for that assignment. Our policies, procedures and assignment instructions do not form part of it unless it says so, and we may update them.

This agreement is meant to record what really happens. If the way you are offered or do work changes, tell us, and we will review this agreement with you.
